data.name: Dattu
data.gender_notes: Dattu is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Dattu is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Datta’, which means ‘given’, ‘gifted’, or ‘granted’. In Hindu mythology, Dattatreya is a form of the god Mahadeva, who is believed to be the giver of all knowledge and blessings. The name Dattu symbolizes the divine gift of knowledge, wisdom, and spiritual growth. The name Dattu carries the meaning “God's Gift” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dattu usually hope their child will grow to embody god's gift and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Divine gift of knowledge and wisdom.
data.etymology: Dattu belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's Gift.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dattu total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Dattatreya is a combined form of three deities: Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva. Dattatreya is often depicted as a sage with three eyes and four arms, holding a trident, a conch, a discus, and a lotus flower. The legend of Dattatreya is said to have originated in the Indian subcontinent around the 1st millennium AD.

Another reference to the name Dattu can be found in the ancient Indian epic, the Mahabharata. In this text, Dattu is mentioned as a king of the Nishada tribe who ruled in the area of modern-day Bihar. He is known for his valor and his alliance with the Pandava brothers during the Mahabharata war, which is believed to have taken place around the 4th century BC.
